title: Lord, Let Our Eyes the Things Unseen Behold
description: Lord, Let Our Eyes the Things Unseen Behold in Tonic Solfa to EVENTIDE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911), headed “Aspirations”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Tens (10.10.10.10), and this page sets them to EVENTIDE; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, let our eyes the things un-seen be-hold, And, 'mid the glo-ry that like sun-set dies, Fair to the sight the won-drous bliss un-fold That lives in beau-ty un-der cloud-less skies.

lines: Lord, let our eyes the things unseen behold,
And, 'mid the glory that like sunset dies,
Fair to the sight the wondrous bliss unfold
That lives in beauty under cloudless skies.
And let our ears the things unuttered hear,
That silent voices to the soul can tell;
That heart can whisper when a heart is near
Of love that scorns in uttered tones to dwell.
Teach us to know that things unseen are real,
That earth no bloom of fadeless beauty gives,
That far beyond the things that sense can feel,
The joy of being, and of having, lives.
Lord Who hast risen, nor left the world behind,
Daily incline our sense-bound souls to soar,
Till 'mong the things all hidden we may find

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to EVENTIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
